boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Samford University
boards.description: Ten under-21-safe Birmingham-area food destinations with currently posted late hours.

cards.title: Taco Bell on Palisades Boulevard
cards.subtitle: 381 Palisades Blvd, Birmingham, AL 35209
cards.notes: Use the drive-thru when you need a late food option; confirm the posted schedule before leaving, especially on holidays.
cards.short_summary: A Birmingham Taco Bell with drive-thru service listed into the early morning.
cards.evidence_claim: The official location page lists drive-thru hours until 3 AM Sunday–Thursday and 4 AM Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru is listed until 3 AM Sunday–Thursday and 4 AM Friday–Saturday; dine-in hours end earlier.

cards.title: Taco Bell in Homewood
cards.subtitle: 159 State Farm Parkway, Homewood, AL 35209
cards.notes: Plan this as a drive-thru stop after evening plans; check the official page for any holiday-hour changes before heading out.
cards.short_summary: A nearby Homewood Taco Bell whose drive-thru runs later than its dining room.
cards.evidence_claim: The official location page lists drive-thru hours until 2 AM Sunday–Thursday and 4 AM Friday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell — 159 State Farm Parkway, Homewood
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru is listed until 2 AM Sunday–Thursday and 4 AM Friday–Saturday; dine-in hours end earlier.

cards.title: Taco Bell on 7th Avenue South
cards.subtitle: 2124 7th Ave S, Birmingham, AL 35233
cards.notes: Treat this as a late drive-thru destination near UAB; use the official hours page to verify the night you plan to go.
cards.short_summary: A Southside Taco Bell with posted drive-thru service into the early morning.
cards.evidence_claim: The official location page lists drive-thru hours until 3 AM on Sunday–Tuesday and 4 AM Wednesday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru is listed until 3 AM Sunday–Tuesday and 4 AM Wednesday–Saturday; dine-in hours end earlier.

cards.title: Taco Bell on Highway 280
cards.subtitle: 4623 Highway 280 S, Birmingham, AL 35242
cards.notes: Check the live location listing before starting the trip, then use the drive-thru for a late food stop along Highway 280.
cards.short_summary: A Highway 280 Taco Bell listed as open late with drive-thru service.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell’s official Birmingham location directory identifies the 4623 Highway 280 S location as open late and lists it open until 3 AM.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell Restaurants in Birmingham, Alabama
cards.access_notes: The official directory lists this location as open until 3 AM; check its individual location page for the day’s schedule.

cards.title: Wendy’s on Valley Avenue
cards.subtitle: 345 Valley Ave, Birmingham, AL 35209
cards.notes: Use this Valley Avenue location for a midnight food stop; its posted restaurant and drive-thru schedules both run to midnight.
cards.short_summary: A Valley Avenue Wendy’s with both service formats listed through midnight.
cards.evidence_claim: The official location page lists restaurant and drive-thru hours of 6:30 AM–12 AM daily.
cards.access_notes: Restaurant and drive-thru are listed open until 12 AM daily; holiday hours may vary.

cards.title: Wendy’s on 7th Avenue South
cards.subtitle: 2327 7th Ave S, Birmingham, AL 35233
cards.notes: Check the posted night-specific hours before leaving; both dining and drive-thru remain available after midnight on the official schedule.
cards.short_summary: A Southside Wendy’s with weekday service listed until 1 AM and weekend service until 2 AM.
cards.evidence_claim: The official location page lists restaurant and drive-thru hours until 1 AM Sunday–Thursday and 2 AM Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Restaurant and drive-thru are listed until 1 AM Sunday–Thursday and 2 AM Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: McDonald’s on 5th Avenue South
cards.subtitle: 1501 5th Ave S, Birmingham, AL 35203
cards.notes: Use the drive-thru for the latest access at this Southside location; the dining room has an earlier listed closing time.
cards.short_summary: A Birmingham McDonald’s with a 24-hour drive-thru schedule.
cards.evidence_claim: The official location page lists its drive-thru as open 24 hours daily, while the lobby is listed until midnight.
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru is listed open 24 hours daily; lobby is listed 5 AM–12 AM daily.

cards.title: McDonald’s on Forestdale Boulevard
cards.subtitle: 1309 Forestdale Blvd, Birmingham, AL 35214
cards.notes: For a late drive-thru option, check the day-specific schedule first; its overnight availability is posted for Thursday through Saturday.
cards.short_summary: A Birmingham McDonald’s with 24-hour drive-thru service on selected nights.
cards.evidence_claim: The official location page lists 24-hour drive-thru service Thursday through Saturday and 11 PM closing Monday–Wednesday and Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru is listed open 24 hours Thursday–Saturday; it is listed until 11 PM Monday–Wednesday and Sunday.

cards.title: Whataburger at Highway 280 and Resource Center
cards.subtitle: 111 Resource Center Pkwy, Birmingham, AL 35242
cards.notes: Use the official locator to confirm holiday operations, then choose curbside, delivery, or an on-site food order at this 24-hour location.
cards.short_summary: A Highway 280 Whataburger listed open around the clock.
cards.evidence_claim: Whataburger’s official Birmingham location directory lists Whataburger #1116 at 111 Resource Center Parkway as open 24 hours every day.
cards.access_notes: Listed open 24 hours daily; the official page notes holiday hours may differ.

cards.title: Rally’s on First Avenue North
cards.subtitle: 4030 First Avenue N, Birmingham, AL 35212
cards.notes: Make this a late food stop rather than a sit-down plan; verify the night’s schedule and use the official ordering options if needed.
cards.short_summary: A First Avenue North Rally’s with service listed until 2 AM most nights and 3 AM on weekends.
cards.evidence_claim: The official location page lists hours until 2 AM Sunday–Thursday and 3 AM Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Listed open until 2 AM Sunday–Thursday and 3 AM Friday–Saturday.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten documented Samford spaces for studying, meals, recreation, and campus gatherings.

cards.entity_name: Harwell G. Davis University Library Third-Floor Study Rooms
cards.title: Third-Floor Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Harwell G. Davis University Library
cards.notes: For a quiet solo or two-person session, ask at the first-floor circulation desk for a key and use the room in two-hour blocks.
cards.short_summary: Individual rooms for one or two Samford students.
cards.evidence_claim: The library says its third-floor study rooms serve one or two Samford students and are available first come, first served.
cards.source_title: Frequently Answered Questions — Samford University Library
cards.access_notes: Samford students; keys are handled through the circulation desk. Check library access and current hours before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Harwell G. Davis University Library Second-Floor Group Study Rooms
cards.title: Second-Floor Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Harwell G. Davis University Library
cards.notes: Bring at least one study partner, then check out a room key from circulation for a focused two-hour group-work block.
cards.short_summary: Locked group rooms designed for two or more students.
cards.evidence_claim: The library policy identifies second-floor study rooms as group spaces for two or more students, with keys checked out at circulation.
cards.source_title: Study Rooms Policy — Samford University Library
cards.access_notes: Available to Samford undergraduate and graduate students; first come, first served, with a two-hour checkout block.

cards.entity_name: Harwell G. Davis University Library Media Rooms 111–115
cards.title: Media Rooms 111–115
cards.subtitle: First floor, Harwell G. Davis University Library
cards.notes: Use these rooms for reserve audiovisual material; group study is possible when other study rooms are full and equipment is not needed.
cards.short_summary: First-floor audiovisual rooms that can accommodate group study.
cards.evidence_claim: The library designates Media Rooms 111–115 for audiovisual use and permits first-come group study when other study rooms are occupied.
cards.source_title: Media Rooms Policy — Samford University Library
cards.access_notes: Academic-media use takes priority; study users may be asked to relocate if equipment is needed.

cards.entity_name: Harwell G. Davis University Library Computer Classroom/Lab
cards.title: Library Computer Classroom/Lab
cards.subtitle: Lower level, Harwell G. Davis University Library
cards.notes: Head to the lower level when you need the library’s mapped computer classroom/lab; confirm building hours before setting up.
cards.short_summary: A mapped lower-level computer space in Davis Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The library’s lower-level floor map lists a Computer Classroom/Lab in the Harwell G. Davis library building.
cards.access_notes: Located on the lower level; library access and hours govern use.

cards.title: Student Commons
cards.subtitle: Ralph W. Beeson University Center
cards.notes: Use the University Center’s student-commons area as a central stop between classes, then check the building’s current access arrangements.
cards.short_summary: A named common area inside Samford’s student-life hub.
cards.evidence_claim: Samford’s event-planning spaces page lists Student Commons in Beeson University Center, and the university describes the center as a hub of student life.
cards.access_notes: Inside the University Center; observe building access and any event reservations.

cards.title: University Center Food Court
cards.subtitle: First floor, Ralph W. Beeson University Center
cards.notes: Meet a classmate for a meal or coffee at the first-floor food court, which Samford lists with several dining counters.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor collection of campus dining counters.
cards.evidence_claim: Samford identifies the Beeson University Center food court as a first-floor location with Boar’s Head, Chick-fil-A, Hissho Sushi, Moe’s, O’Henry’s, Samford Grill, and Simply to Go.
cards.access_notes: Food service is in the University Center; availability may vary with the academic calendar.

cards.title: The Caf
cards.subtitle: Ralph W. Beeson University Center
cards.notes: Plan a campus meal at The Caf, then review dining access or meal-plan details through Samford before relying on it.
cards.short_summary: The University Center’s mapped dining hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Samford’s campus map lists The Caf as the Dining Hall within Ralph W. Beeson University Center.
cards.access_notes: Located in Beeson University Center; dining access and service vary by university schedule.

cards.title: Seibert Hall
cards.subtitle: Campus Recreation, Wellness and Athletics Complex
cards.notes: Choose a court, track, studio, billiards table, or fitness area for a recreation break; verify the current facility schedule first.
cards.short_summary: A four-story recreation complex with courts, studios, and shared activity areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Samford says Seibert Hall contains courts, fitness areas, an elevated jogging track, studios, billiards, a coffeehouse, and a 24-hour market.
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to Campus Recreation membership, guest rules, event reservations, and changing hours.

cards.title: Intramural Fields
cards.subtitle: Intramural/Recreation Complex
cards.notes: Join an outdoor intramural game or use the courts and covered pavilion when the area is available through Campus Recreation.
cards.short_summary: Outdoor fields with student recreation facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: Samford identifies the intramural fields as the home for outdoor intramurals and lists soccer, flag football, softball, Ultimate Frisbee, sand volleyball, basketball, and a covered pavilion.
cards.access_notes: Coordinate with Campus Recreation and observe field availability for intramural or informal use.

cards.title: Reid Chapel
cards.subtitle: Samford University campus
cards.notes: Check the university calendar for a convocation or concert, then arrive through the appropriate public entrance for that event.
cards.short_summary: A campus chapel used for convocations and concerts.
cards.evidence_claim: Samford describes A. Hamilton Reid Chapel as the site of many convocations and concerts.
cards.access_notes: Event attendance and building access depend on the scheduled program.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-admission places for a walk, conversation, or self-guided look at plants and art near Samford.

cards.title: Walk the Japanese Garden
cards.subtitle: Birmingham Botanical Gardens, 2612 Lane Park Road
cards.notes: Meet at the garden entrance, stroll its paths at an unhurried pace, and use the map to pick a nearby second garden before leaving.
cards.short_summary: A named garden space for a low-key outdoor walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Birmingham Botanical Gardens states that general admission is free and the Japanese Garden is one of its named garden spaces.
cards.source_title: Explore our Gardens | Birmingham Botanical Gardens
cards.access_notes: The Gardens are free and open to the public every day of the year; visit during posted garden hours.

cards.title: Look for native plants in Kaul
cards.subtitle: Birmingham Botanical Gardens, 2612 Lane Park Road
cards.notes: Use the garden map to find Kaul Wildflower Garden, then take a slow loop and compare the plants you notice with a friend.
cards.short_summary: A named wildflower garden within the free public Gardens.
cards.evidence_claim: Birmingham Botanical Gardens states that general admission is free and lists Kaul Wildflower Garden among its garden spaces.
cards.source_title: Explore our Gardens | Birmingham Botanical Gardens
cards.access_notes: The Gardens are free and open to the public every day of the year; visit during posted garden hours.

cards.title: Pause by the Echo pool
cards.subtitle: Southern Living Garden, Birmingham Botanical Gardens
cards.notes: Find the Echo Reflecting Pool and Terrace, take one of the benches, and use the setting for a relaxed catch-up or a few quiet minutes.
cards.short_summary: A named garden with a reflecting pool, terrace, and benches.
cards.evidence_claim: Birmingham Botanical Gardens states that general admission is free; its Southern Living Garden page identifies the Echo Reflecting Pool and Terrace.
cards.source_title: Southern Living Garden | Birmingham Botanical Gardens
cards.access_notes: The Gardens are free and open to the public every day of the year; visit during posted garden hours.

cards.title: Visit the Conservatory
cards.subtitle: Birmingham Botanical Gardens, 2612 Lane Park Road
cards.notes: Locate the Conservatory on the official garden map and make it a short indoor-outdoor stop paired with the adjacent formal garden spaces.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed Conservatory at the free public Gardens.
cards.evidence_claim: Birmingham Botanical Gardens states that general admission is free and lists the Conservatory as a garden destination.
cards.source_title: Explore our Gardens | Birmingham Botanical Gardens
cards.access_notes: The Gardens are free and open to the public every day of the year; visit during posted garden hours.

cards.title: Tour the Bruno Vegetable Garden
cards.subtitle: Birmingham Botanical Gardens, 2612 Lane Park Road
cards.notes: Use the official map to locate the vegetable garden and herb terrace, then walk through together and note plants you would like to grow.
cards.short_summary: A named vegetable-garden stop at the free public Gardens.
cards.evidence_claim: Birmingham Botanical Gardens states that general admission is free and lists Bruno Vegetable Garden among its garden spaces.
cards.source_title: Explore our Gardens | Birmingham Botanical Gardens
cards.access_notes: The Gardens are free and open to the public every day of the year; visit during posted garden hours.

cards.title: Make a lakeside walking stop
cards.subtitle: Sonat Lake, Birmingham Botanical Gardens
cards.notes: Use the visitor map to reach Sonat Lake, then take a lap through the nearby paths and choose a second garden to explore.
cards.short_summary: A named lake on the official Birmingham Botanical Gardens map.
cards.evidence_claim: Birmingham Botanical Gardens states that general admission is free and its official visitor map lists Sonat Lake.
cards.access_notes: The Gardens are free and open to the public every day of the year; visit during posted garden hours.

cards.title: Take a rose-garden loop
cards.subtitle: Dunn Formal Rose Garden, Birmingham Botanical Gardens
cards.notes: Find the formal rose garden on the visitor map, walk its borders together, and pair it with the nearby Ireland Old-Fashioned Rose Garden.
cards.short_summary: A named formal rose garden at the free public Gardens.
cards.evidence_claim: Birmingham Botanical Gardens states that general admission is free and lists Dunn Formal Rose Garden among its garden spaces.
cards.source_title: Explore our Gardens | Birmingham Botanical Gardens
cards.access_notes: The Gardens are free and open to the public every day of the year; visit during posted garden hours.

cards.title: Walk through Fern Glade
cards.subtitle: Birmingham Botanical Gardens, 2612 Lane Park Road
cards.notes: Use the official garden list and map to find Fern Glade, then keep the visit simple with a slow walk and a few plant photos.
cards.short_summary: A named fern-filled garden space at the free public Gardens.
cards.evidence_claim: Birmingham Botanical Gardens states that general admission is free and lists Fern Glade among its garden spaces.
cards.source_title: Explore our Gardens | Birmingham Botanical Gardens
cards.access_notes: The Gardens are free and open to the public every day of the year; visit during posted garden hours.

cards.title: Sit near Curry Pond
cards.subtitle: Curry Rhododendron Garden, Birmingham Botanical Gardens
cards.notes: Walk to Curry Pond and its rocky waterfall, then use a nearby bench for conversation before continuing through the surrounding garden paths.
cards.short_summary: A named rhododendron garden with Curry Pond and a waterfall.
cards.evidence_claim: Birmingham Botanical Gardens states that general admission is free; its Curry Rhododendron Garden page identifies Curry Pond and its rocky waterfall.
cards.source_title: Curry Rhododendron Garden | Birmingham Botanical Gardens
cards.access_notes: The Gardens are free and open to the public every day of the year; visit during posted garden hours.

cards.title: Browse the collection galleries
cards.subtitle: 2000 Reverend Abraham Woods Jr. Boulevard, Birmingham
cards.notes: Choose a collection-gallery wing, move at your own pace, and compare one artwork each before regrouping in the museum’s public spaces.
cards.short_summary: A downtown art-museum visit with free general admission.
cards.evidence_claim: The Birmingham Museum of Art says general admission is always free and includes all collection galleries and most exhibitions.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Birmingham Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: General admission is always free; check the museum’s current posted hours and closure notices before going.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten named Samford study settings with documented room features, locations, and use rules.

cards.title: Third-Floor Individual Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Harwell G. Davis Library · third floor
cards.notes: Ask at the first-floor Circulation Desk for a key, then use an individual room for up to two hours; renew only if no one is waiting.
cards.short_summary: Locked individual rooms for one or two Samford students.
cards.evidence_claim: Davis Library's third-floor study rooms are for individual use by one or two Samford students and are first-come, first-served.
cards.source_title: Study Rooms Policy | Samford University Library
cards.access_notes: Available to Samford undergraduate and graduate students, excluding Law students; keys are checked out at Circulation for two-hour blocks and rooms cannot be reserved.

cards.title: Study Room 211
cards.subtitle: Harwell G. Davis Library · second floor
cards.notes: Bring a study partner and request this Solstice-equipped room at Circulation when you need to share a laptop or mobile screen.
cards.short_summary: A group room with a Solstice Pod and wall-mounted display.
cards.evidence_claim: Study Room 211 is equipped with a Solstice Pod and wall-mounted flat-panel display for sharing media from laptops or mobile devices.
cards.source_title: Study Rooms Policy | Samford University Library
cards.access_notes: Second-floor group rooms require two or more Samford undergraduate or graduate students; obtain a key at Circulation, first come first served, for a two-hour block.

cards.title: Study Room 217
cards.subtitle: Harwell G. Davis Library · second floor
cards.notes: Use this display-equipped room for a shared slide deck or media review; pick up the key from Circulation before settling in.
cards.short_summary: A second-floor group room set up for screen sharing.
cards.evidence_claim: Study Room 217 is equipped with a Solstice Pod and wall-mounted flat-panel display; Solstice supports laptop and mobile media sharing.
cards.source_title: Study Rooms Policy | Samford University Library
cards.access_notes: Group study rooms are for two or more eligible Samford students, are not reservable, and use first-come, first-served two-hour key checkout.

cards.title: Study Room 236
cards.subtitle: Harwell G. Davis Library · second floor
cards.notes: Coordinate with your group, then request this room at Circulation for a focused work block with a wall-mounted display.
cards.short_summary: A group study room with built-in Solstice display sharing.
cards.evidence_claim: Study Room 236 has a Solstice Pod and wall-mounted flat-panel display, with HDMI connection available in the room.
cards.source_title: Study Rooms Policy | Samford University Library
cards.access_notes: For groups of at least two eligible Samford undergraduate or graduate students; obtain a two-hour key checkout at the first-floor Circulation Desk.

cards.title: Media Room 111
cards.subtitle: Harwell G. Davis Library · first floor
cards.notes: Use the audiovisual setup for reserve material; group study is possible only when other study rooms are full and equipment is not needed.
cards.short_summary: A small media room with audiovisual playback equipment.
cards.evidence_claim: Media Room 111 is on Davis Library's first floor, holds one to four people, and has television, DVD, VHS, record-player, and sound-system equipment.
cards.source_title: Media Rooms Policy | Samford University Library
cards.access_notes: Media rooms primarily support audiovisual reserve or academic media. Group study is first come first served only if other study rooms are occupied and the equipment is not needed.

cards.title: Media Room 112
cards.subtitle: Harwell G. Davis Library · first floor
cards.notes: Choose this compact room when your assignment needs library audiovisual equipment, and be prepared to relocate if reserve viewing takes priority.
cards.short_summary: A one-to-four-person media room for academic viewing or listening.
cards.evidence_claim: Media Room 112 is a first-floor Davis Library media room with capacity for one to four people and connected audiovisual equipment.
cards.source_title: Media Rooms Policy | Samford University Library
cards.access_notes: First come first served for group study only when all study rooms are occupied and no patron needs the room's audiovisual equipment for reserve material.

cards.title: Media Room 113
cards.subtitle: Harwell G. Davis Library · first floor
cards.notes: Bring a small group for course media or reserve viewing; confirm that the room is not needed for equipment-based use before studying.
cards.short_summary: A media-enabled room sized for two to seven people.
cards.evidence_claim: Media Room 113 is located on the first floor of Davis Library and has capacity for two to seven people.
cards.source_title: Media Rooms Policy | Samford University Library
cards.access_notes: The room is designated for audiovisual reserve or academic media; group study is first come first served only when other study rooms are occupied and equipment use is not needed.

cards.title: Media Room 114
cards.subtitle: Harwell G. Davis Library · first floor
cards.notes: Set up a course-media session for a mid-sized group, keeping plans flexible because academic equipment use takes priority in this room.
cards.short_summary: A two-to-seven-person room with connected media equipment.
cards.evidence_claim: Media Room 114 is a first-floor Davis Library room for two to seven people with television, DVD, VHS, record-player, and sound-system equipment.
cards.source_title: Media Rooms Policy | Samford University Library
cards.access_notes: Group study is permitted first come first served only if all other study rooms are occupied and no one needs the room to use audiovisual equipment.

cards.title: Media Room 115
cards.subtitle: Harwell G. Davis Library · first floor
cards.notes: Use the largest listed media room for a course viewing or substantial group session, while yielding it when reserve-media equipment is requested.
cards.short_summary: A larger first-floor media room for up to twenty people.
cards.evidence_claim: Media Room 115 is on the first floor of Davis Library, has capacity for two to twenty people, and includes connected audiovisual equipment.
cards.source_title: Media Rooms Policy | Samford University Library
cards.access_notes: The room is for audiovisual equipment and academic media; it may be used for group study first come first served only when other study rooms are occupied and equipment is not needed.

cards.title: OBB 300
cards.subtitle: Education Learning Commons · Orlean Bullard Beeson Hall
cards.notes: Reserve OBB 300 through SPACES when you need an open collaboration setting with multiple screens and wireless display sharing.
cards.short_summary: An open study and collaboration area with three televisions.
cards.evidence_claim: OBB 300 is a relaxed, open area for studying, working, and collaboration with two 52-inch televisions, a smart television, and Mersive Solstice sharing.
cards.access_notes: Located on the third floor of Orlean Bullard Beeson Hall. The Education Learning Commons follows the academic calendar; OBB 300 can be reserved through SPACES.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named, public-facing destinations along the Homewood corridors in Samford’s practical orbit, each with one source-supported reason to stop.

cards.title: Central Park — walking paths and open lawn
cards.subtitle: Oxmoor Road corridor
cards.notes: Bring a book or a friend and use the cement walking paths, open green space, playground, or amphitheater; review park rules before planning a gathering.
cards.short_summary: A city park with paths, lawn, courts, and six picnic pavilions.
cards.evidence_claim: Homewood Parks & Recreation lists Central Park at 1632 Oxmoor Road with cement walking paths, open green space, a playground, amphitheater, tennis courts, and six picnic pavilions.
cards.access_notes: Park rules state it closes at 10:00 p.m. unless otherwise approved by the Parks & Recreation Board.

cards.title: Homewood Public Library — an evening reading stop
cards.subtitle: Oxmoor Road corridor
cards.notes: Check the library calendar, then settle in with a book or use a listed service such as printing or the Makery during its posted public hours.
cards.short_summary: A public library on Oxmoor Road with several late weekday evenings.
cards.evidence_claim: Homewood Public Library lists its address as 1721 Oxmoor Road and posts Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday hours of 9 a.m.–9 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Posted hours vary by day; confirm the library calendar and closure list before visiting.

cards.title: Sims Garden — self-guided botanical paths
cards.subtitle: Highland Road / Irving Road corridor
cards.notes: Take a self-guided walk through the botanical park, look for its public art and garden features, and pick available produce only from designated beds.
cards.short_summary: A city-maintained botanical garden open daily for self-guided tours.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Homewood says Sims Garden spans five lots between 908 Highland Road and 913 Irving Road and is open daily for self-guided tours.
cards.access_notes: The city notes that fruit and vegetables may be picked from designated Grow More, Give More beds when available.

cards.title: Homewood City Hall — civic-information stop
cards.subtitle: 19th Street South corridor
cards.notes: Use the city’s posted contact point to find meeting, service, or department information, then pair the stop with a walk through the surrounding downtown blocks.
cards.short_summary: The municipal hub for city departments, services, meetings, and agendas.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Homewood lists City Hall at 2850 19th Street South and links municipal meetings, agendas, departments, and public services from its site.
cards.access_notes: City Hall lists Monday–Friday office hours of 8:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m. on the cited city page.

cards.title: Big Spoon Creamery — a dessert stop
cards.subtitle: Oxmoor Road corridor
cards.notes: Check the current flavor board and posted hours before heading to the Homewood shop; it is a straightforward option for an ice-cream break on Oxmoor Road.
cards.short_summary: A Homewood ice-cream shop with posted daily service hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Big Spoon Creamery lists its Homewood location at 927 Oxmoor Road and posts noon–9 p.m. Sunday–Thursday and noon–10 p.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Hours are posted by the business and may change; verify before leaving campus.

cards.title: O.Henry’s Coffee — locally roasted coffee
cards.subtitle: 18th Street South corridor
cards.notes: Meet over coffee or take a short reset at the Homewood location; use the business’s location page to confirm the day’s hours before walking over.
cards.short_summary: A Birmingham coffee roaster with a Homewood shop on 18th Street South.
cards.evidence_claim: O.Henry’s lists its Homewood location at 2831 18th Street South and describes its coffee as roasted locally in Birmingham.
cards.access_notes: The business posts Homewood hours of 6 a.m.–6 p.m. Monday–Saturday and 7 a.m.–6 p.m. Sunday.

cards.title: Edgar’s Bakery — bakery counter and kitchen
cards.subtitle: 18th Street South corridor
cards.notes: Choose a bakery item or daytime meal from the Homewood counter, and check the location page first because the store and kitchen have separately posted hours.
cards.short_summary: A Homewood bakery location serving bakery items and kitchen fare.
cards.evidence_claim: Edgar’s Bakery lists its Homewood location at 2713 18th Street South, with store hours Monday–Saturday, 7 a.m.–6 p.m.
cards.access_notes: The cited page lists the Homewood kitchen hours as 7 a.m.–3 p.m., Monday–Saturday.

cards.title: Johnny’s Restaurant — Greek-and-three lunch
cards.subtitle: 18th Street South corridor
cards.notes: Plan this as a lunch stop and consult the restaurant’s posted schedule before going; the Homewood address is in Suite 200 on 18th Street South.
cards.short_summary: A Homewood lunch restaurant with a Greek-and-three identity.
cards.evidence_claim: Johnny’s identifies itself as “Johnny’s Greek And Three” and lists its restaurant at 2902 18th Street South, Suite 200, Homewood.
cards.access_notes: Posted lunch hours are Monday–Friday and Sunday, 11 a.m.–2:30 p.m.; it is closed Saturday.

cards.title: Homewood Gourmet — fast-casual food
cards.subtitle: Mamie L Foster / 18th Place South corridor
cards.notes: Use the restaurant’s current menu to choose a sandwich, salad, or prepared dinner item, then visit during its listed daytime service window.
cards.short_summary: A locally owned fast-casual restaurant on 18th Place South.
cards.evidence_claim: Homewood Gourmet says it is a locally owned fast-casual restaurant at 2703 Mamie L Foster, 18th Place, Homewood, and lists sandwiches, salads, and dinner entrées to go.
cards.source_title: Homewood Gourmet | Restaurant in Homewood, AL
cards.access_notes: Posted hours are Monday–Friday 10:30 a.m.–6 p.m. and Saturday 10:30 a.m.–2 p.m.; it is closed Sunday.

cards.title: Little Donkey — Mexican menu stop
cards.subtitle: 18th Street South corridor
cards.notes: Browse the restaurant’s current online menu before visiting, then use its posted Homewood address and hours to plan a meal stop on the 18th Street South block.
cards.short_summary: A Homewood restaurant with a Mexican menu and online ordering.
cards.evidence_claim: Little Donkey’s official ordering page identifies the Homewood restaurant at 2701 18th Street South, Suite 200, and categorizes it as Mexican.
cards.access_notes: Use the restaurant’s official ordering page to confirm current service availability before visiting.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Samford traditions, from student-produced Step Sing rituals to campus gatherings across the academic year.

cards.title: Step Sing
cards.subtitle: Student-produced singing and dance competition
cards.notes: Attend a performance to see student groups combine musical arrangement, choreography, costumes and a themed production.
cards.short_summary: A Samford competition that grew from a 1951 sing-along into a large student-organized show.
cards.evidence_claim: Samford says Step Sing began as a 1951 sing-along and is organized by students who handle musical arrangement, choreography and costume design.
cards.access_notes: Held at the Wright Center; consult the event page for current performance details.

cards.title: Step Sing Banner Drop
cards.subtitle: The Step Sing season opener at the Wright Center
cards.notes: Watch each participating group reveal its banner and show title, then look for the banners when they move to later displays.
cards.short_summary: A reveal event where Step Sing groups drop banners and disclose their show themes.
cards.evidence_claim: Samford's 2026 Step Sing program describes Banner Drop as the event that officially starts the season, with groups dropping banners to reveal titles and themes.
cards.access_notes: The program identifies the Wright Center as the Banner Drop venue.

cards.title: Step Sing Signature Moves
cards.subtitle: Recognizable gestures tied to participating groups
cards.notes: During performances, notice recurring gestures or short sequences and the onstage shout-outs that reference another group’s move.
cards.short_summary: Groups build recognizable choreographic calling cards into Step Sing culture.
cards.evidence_claim: Samford's 2026 Step Sing program says participating groups develop recognizable signature gestures or short choreographed sequences and may incorporate another group's move as a shout-out.
cards.access_notes: See this as part of a Step Sing performance; individual groups determine their own moves.

cards.title: Connections Weekend
cards.subtitle: New-student welcome tradition
cards.notes: New students are placed in upperclassman-led small groups for campus and Birmingham introductions, mixers and other scheduled events.
cards.short_summary: A structured first-weekend welcome that connects incoming students with peers and campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Samford calls Connections Weekend a beloved tradition for new students and says each student is placed in a small group led by upperclassmen.
cards.access_notes: Samford states new students are automatically registered; view the current Connections information for programming.

cards.title: Bulldog Walk
cards.subtitle: Home-football pregame walk
cards.notes: Arrive before a home kickoff to line the route from the University Center toward the Sullivan-Cooney Family Fieldhouse.
cards.short_summary: A pregame procession that sends the football team from the University Center toward the fieldhouse.
cards.evidence_claim: Samford identifies Bulldog Walk as a tailgate tradition that begins two hours before home-game kickoff at the University Center's south entrance and ends at Sullivan-Cooney Family Fieldhouse.
cards.access_notes: Samford schedules it for all home games, beginning two hours before kickoff.

cards.title: Homecoming Board Displays
cards.subtitle: Student-organization displays on Ben Brown Plaza
cards.notes: Walk Ben Brown Plaza during Homecoming to view the decorated boards created by participating student organizations.
cards.short_summary: A visual Homecoming tradition in which organizations create displays for campus visitors.
cards.evidence_claim: Samford reports that student organizations decorate Homecoming Board Displays and display them on Ben Brown Plaza throughout Homecoming weekend.
cards.access_notes: Available during Homecoming weekend; the article locates the boards on Ben Brown Plaza.

cards.title: Alumni Candlelight Dinner and Awards
cards.subtitle: Homecoming recognition tradition
cards.notes: Check the Homecoming schedule for this alumni gathering, which recognizes service and distinguished careers through three award categories.
cards.short_summary: A Homecoming dinner and awards ceremony with roots reaching to the 1860s.
cards.evidence_claim: Samford describes the Alumni Candlelight Dinner and Awards as a time-honored tradition dating to the 1860s that recognizes alumni in three categories.
cards.access_notes: This is part of Homecoming programming; current attendance details depend on the annual schedule.

cards.title: Lighting of the Way
cards.subtitle: Centennial Walk Christmas tree lighting
cards.notes: Join the December countdown on Centennial Walk, with the Christmas story, carols, tree lighting and a closing concert.
cards.short_summary: A December gathering built around luminaries, carols and the Centennial Walk tree.
cards.evidence_claim: Samford says Lighting of the Way lines the quad with luminaries and culminates in a Christmas-story reading, carols, tree lighting and concert.
cards.access_notes: Samford describes it as occurring at the start of the Christmas season on Centennial Walk.

cards.title: Your School Your City
cards.subtitle: Fall welcome concert and Birmingham introduction
cards.notes: Visit the Quad concert and browse the local-business tents to learn about Birmingham-area options during the fall welcome week.
cards.short_summary: A fall campus welcome that introduces students to Birmingham through a Quad concert and local vendors.
cards.evidence_claim: Samford says Your School Your City introduces students to Birmingham and surrounding communities through a Quad concert and tents from local businesses and restaurants.
cards.access_notes: Samford places this event each fall; consult the full event calendar for current details.

cards.title: Spring Fling
cards.subtitle: End-of-classes outdoor campus gathering
cards.notes: Look for the end-of-classes program on Ben Brown Plaza and the Quad, with outdoor activities, food trucks and a concert.
cards.short_summary: A late-spring student gathering intended to mark the close of classes before finals.
cards.evidence_claim: Samford's Student Government page describes Spring Fling as a program in the last three days of classes with outdoor activities, food trucks and an outdoor concert.
cards.access_notes: Samford describes Spring Fling as taking place during the final three class days; verify the annual schedule.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Samford University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A simple, under-21-safe sequence for getting oriented on campus, finding shared spaces, and taking one nearby daytime walk.

cards.title: Start with a campus walk
cards.subtitle: First stop: Centennial Walk
cards.notes: Begin by walking Centennial Walk and use the campus tour map to orient yourself before choosing a study spot or meeting up with new classmates.
cards.short_summary: A named virtual-tour stop for an unhurried first look at central campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Samford’s undergraduate virtual tour lists Centennial Walk as a tour stop.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus route; follow posted campus access guidance.

cards.title: Find your library bearings
cards.subtitle: Next: Davis University Library
cards.notes: Step into the library, locate the circulation area, and note the second-floor group study rooms and third-floor individual study rooms for later.
cards.short_summary: A campus library stop with mapped study spaces on multiple floors.
cards.evidence_claim: The library’s floor maps identify group study rooms on the second floor and individual study rooms on the third floor.
cards.access_notes: Use the library’s posted access information; an accessible east-side entrance is described on its floor-maps page.

cards.title: Pause at Ben Brown Plaza
cards.subtitle: Then: between the University Center and Library
cards.notes: Take a short pause at the plaza, check what is happening around you, and use it as a low-pressure place to reconnect with people from move-in.
cards.short_summary: A central outdoor gathering place between two key campus buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: Samford identifies Ben Brown Plaza, between the University Center and Library, as its primary student gathering place and a site for events.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor plaza; events and access can vary.

cards.title: Locate everyday essentials
cards.subtitle: Midday: Beeson University Center
cards.notes: Make a quick loop through the University Center to find the HUB, post office, bookstore, student-life offices, lounges, and dining areas.
cards.short_summary: A practical orientation stop for student services and shared indoor spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Samford says the University Center houses the HUB, bookstore, post office, career development, student-life offices, Caf, food court and lounges.
cards.access_notes: Indoor building; verify current departmental and dining access before visiting.

cards.title: Choose a casual meal stop
cards.subtitle: Lunch: University Center Food Court
cards.notes: Use the food court for a straightforward lunch while you compare campus options and make plans for the rest of the afternoon with your group.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus food court with several named vendors.
cards.evidence_claim: Samford lists Boar's Head Deli, Chick-fil-A, Hissho Sushi, Moe's Southwest Grill, O'Henry's coffee, Samford Grill and Simply to Go in the food court.
cards.access_notes: Food purchases or a meal plan may be required; vendor availability can change.

cards.title: See Reid Chapel from the quad
cards.subtitle: Afternoon: Reid Chapel
cards.notes: Walk by Reid Chapel and check the campus calendar if you want to return for an appropriate public convocation or concert during the semester.
cards.short_summary: A prominent campus chapel used for convocations and concerts.
cards.evidence_claim: Samford states that Reid Chapel is a campus landmark and the site of many convocations and concerts.
cards.access_notes: View exterior freely; attendance or interior access depends on scheduled events and campus guidance.

cards.title: Visit Hodges Chapel thoughtfully
cards.subtitle: Next: Andrew Gerow Hodges Chapel
cards.notes: If the chapel is open, take time to view its interior respectfully and read about the figures represented there; do not interrupt services or private use.
cards.short_summary: A consecrated chapel with an ornate interior and Baptist-history imagery.
cards.evidence_claim: Samford says Hodges Chapel was consecrated in 1995 and that its interior depicts 16 figures in Protestant and Baptist development.
cards.access_notes: Respect worship and event use; interior availability is not guaranteed.

cards.title: Add a quiet gallery visit
cards.subtitle: Late afternoon: Swearingen Hall
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition before heading over, then spend a few minutes with the work and look for any listed artist talk, workshop, or campus event.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated exhibition space for student, faculty, and guest-artist work.
cards.evidence_claim: Samford describes the Samford Art Gallery as a dedicated exhibition space and states it is free to the public Monday through Friday, 9 a.m.–4 p.m.
cards.source_title: Facilities - School of the Arts | Samford University
cards.access_notes: Official page lists Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–4 p.m.; confirm exhibition and holiday access before going.

cards.title: Try the recreation center
cards.subtitle: Early evening: Seibert Hall
cards.notes: Bring your Samford ID if required, review current facility rules, and choose a low-key workout or recreation activity that fits your energy and schedule.
cards.short_summary: A campus recreation stop with a currently posted summer operating schedule.
cards.evidence_claim: Samford Campus Recreation posts Seibert Hall operating hours and notes that hours can change with the university calendar and events.
cards.access_notes: The posted 2026 summer schedule lists Saturday 10 a.m.–4 p.m. and Sunday 2–8 p.m.; hours can change, so verify before visiting.

cards.title: Close with a daytime garden walk
cards.subtitle: Off-campus daytime option: Birmingham Botanical Gardens
cards.notes: For a calm Sunday outing, walk the gardens in daylight, use the official map to pick a section, and leave time to return before closing.
cards.short_summary: A nearby public garden with free admission and free parking.
cards.evidence_claim: Birmingham Botanical Gardens states that general admission and parking are free and that the gardens are open every day of the year.
cards.access_notes: For Aug. 13, 2026, the official spring/summer schedule lists 7 a.m.–7 p.m. daily; seasonal hours change.
